collection_method: Read-only GitHub repository, issue-search, issue and comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. The former Strands Python SDK path was resolved as a repository redirect to strands-agents/harness-sdk. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and not executed. No packages, agents, models, tools, workflows, MCP servers, graphs or target systems were run or contacted.

selected_records.title: [BUG] on_error='proceed' silently bypasses a handler-raised approval pause, running the tool unapproved
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled human-approval bypass under non-default error handling
selected_records.provider_attribution: Strands Python intervention registry with a scripted local model; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic keyless test reports a handler-raised approval pause being swallowed under on_error='proceed', allowing the sensitive tool to run. The issue closed two days later. This is a single-agent authorization control, not a participant exchange.

selected_records.title: [BUG] Graph treats a cancelled child AgentResult as completed and routes downstream
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled cancellation boundary ignored by downstream routing
selected_records.provider_attribution: Strands Python multi-agent graph with mock agents; no model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: Project automation independently reproduced a deterministic test in which a cancelled child is marked completed and its downstream node executes. The record explicitly disclaims a security claim and uses configured graph nodes, so it is a routing control rather than a rogue episode.

selected_records.title: [Bug] Parallel invocations to the same Agent instance corrupt message history
selected_records.provider_attribution: Strands Agent instance; maintainers mention downstream Bedrock validation errors but no provider-side fault.
selected_records.assessment: A maintainer says multiple customers reported overlapping invocations corrupting shared message history, most visibly as later validation failures, and that a guard shipped in version 1.22. This is one shared agent instance, not distinct participants or a task-result handoff.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: ReActAgent handoff leaves stale current_reasoning in ctx.store, contaminating the next turn's prompt and memory
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled cross-agent and cross-turn reasoning contamination
selected_records.provider_attribution: LlamaIndex AgentWorkflow with deterministic mock models; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic two-agent test shows a handing-off ReAct agent's reasoning remaining in shared context, entering the receiving agent's prompt, contaminating the next turn and being stored as the wrong assistant answer. It is strong transfer/use evidence in a designed workflow, not independently authenticated autonomous coordination.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: AgentWorkflow stores agents by reference; one BaseTool instance shared across agents leaks per-tool mutations
selected_records.provider_attribution: LlamaIndex AgentWorkflow object identity; no provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A local object-identity test shows two configured agents sharing one tool instance also sharing mutable metadata and partial parameters. The issue closed as not planned, and copying live-resource tools has explicit tradeoffs. No actual wrong-agent tool execution or transferred result was demonstrated.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: MCP tool failures are reported to the agent as successes
selected_records.provider_attribution: LlamaIndex MCP integration; no specific MCP server or model provider established.
selected_records.assessment: Static path analysis and public comment review show MCP error status not propagating, so a failed return-direct tool can end a run as apparent success. This is tool-result classification, not a distinct-agent exchange or unauthorized coordination.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. Deterministic tests preserve cancelled-child downstream execution and stale handoff reasoning transfer/use, but all participants are configured graph/workflow roles and every episode was already public.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
Issue bodies, automated project verification and comments are public tracker evidence, not authenticated agent telemetry.
The Strands old repository URL redirects to a monorepo; this resolves the earlier access gap but does not imply the old path was absent.
Configured graph nodes and workflow agents are not independently verified autonomous participants.
Open issue state and later comments do not establish continuing agent activity.
No code, package, reproduction, agent, model, tool, workflow, MCP server, graph or target service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization in a real run.
redactions: No executable reproduction bodies, credentials, private logs, endpoint details, personal addresses or live tool payloads are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing mechanisms at a domain level.
